survey.request: パートごとに演出をそろえ、くり返す歌詞は同じ見せ方で戻ってくる
survey.summary: Repeated lyrics can come back with exactly the same look, but only through the opt-in 「くり返しの行をそろえる」, which is off by default. With it off, only the camera shot is inherited automatically (about 64 % of repeated cuts), and layouts and motions match only 12–16 % of the time. Per-part consistency covers only the camera and background: one 区画のカメラ rig per section, section-weighted shots, and background changes at section boundaries. Layout, motion, decoration, effect and text choices share no family within a section, and there is no mood per section.
evidence: src/planner/cast.js alignments()/decideRepeat()/alignedPart()/alignedValue(): 「くり返しの行をそろえる」 (slot 'repeat.same', SLOT_SPECS). Returns null unless a pin exists (PA.pinned(ctx.ix, REPEAT)), so it is off by default. When on, a copy takes its source's orient, arrange, text.*, motion.speed, arrive/dwell/depart plus params, ornaments, lens, filters and camera.
src/planner/camera.js rigCopy() and src/planner/tracks.js splitSegments()/alignedSource(): under the opt-in, the section rig, background segment, ground/atmos and seam of a copy follow the source.

src/planner/choose.js ECHO = 2.5 (preWeight: req.echo) and src/planner/cast.js createHistory().echo(): the default soft echo for every part slot of a repeated line (feat.repeatOf from src/planner/plan.js featureContexts).
src/planner/camera.js inheritedShot()/heirOf()/SHOT_ECHO = 40 (DESIGN_2_1 §4.7 'Repeated lines' rules 1–6): default-on inheritance of the first copy's cam.shot and cam.curve.

src/planner/camera.js splitRuns()/rigs()/RIG_WEIGHTS/rigRow(): one rig per section run (split where feat.section changes), rows per section kind (chorus slowSwell/climbRise, verse driftSide …); last chorus amp ×1.25 and curve slowBloom.
src/planner/camera.js SHOT_SECTION (chorus pushWord/snapZoom/sweepAcross ×1.5; verse settle/driftOff/none ×1.3; bridge tiltHold/wideHold ×1.5); src/planner/extreme.js SECTION weights.
src/planner/tracks.js breakScore(): +1 when feat.section changes, so backgrounds usually (not always, noise ±0.3) start a new segment at a section boundary.
src/planner/features.js HEADING_SECTIONS/sectionOfHeading()/songSection(): sections come from '#' headings (サビ/Aメロ/Bメロ…) or the AI song analysis (doc.song.info.sections).
src/planner/look.js: mood/theme/amounts are work-level only (no per-section mood).

src/ui/fields.js PAGES.work sec('look') toggle REPEAT_SAME (fld.repeatSame 「くり返しの行をそろえる」, note fld.repeatSame.note); repeatLineField() (fld.repeatSameLine 「くり返しをそろえる」, opt.repeatSame.on/off); PAGES.lines sec('rig') for an area; strings why.repeat.same / whyRule.repeat.same / ai.warn.repeatSame.
src/core/doc / src/core/commands.js: no default pin for new documents; commands refuse cut-scope repeat.same.

Tests: tests/node/repeat_same.test.js (opt-in off = unchanged plan; alignments; neighbours), tests/node/camera_planner.test.js ('repeated lines echo their shot', 'rig runs … follow sections', 'rig choice: the section rows…'), tests/golden/project_repeat.json.

Measured (read-only script $SCRATCH/survey/m1.js, sample lyrics with a second サビ, 4 moods × 2 aspects × 4 seeds, catalog, 384 repeated cuts). Default: same arrange 15.9 %, arrive 12.0 %, lens 19.8 %, ornament#0 13.0 %, cam.shot 64.3 %. With the opt-in: arrange/lens/shot/ornament 100 %, arrive 99.5 %, depart 92.2 %. Within a section, the most common arrange family covers only 22.4 % of cuts vs 19.5 % song-wide, so there is no per-part family concentration.
survey.userPath: 作品全体 › 見た目 › 「くり返しの行をそろえる」 (トグル、既定オフ). Per line: 行 › 演出 (詳細) › 「くり返しをそろえる」 (自動/そろえる/そろえない). Per part, by hand: click a 区画 band in the timeline's 曲 row (サビ1 etc.) → the 「n行を選択中」 page → pin 構図/入り/抜け etc. under 演出（すべてのカット）, and 区画のカメラ. Optional AI: AI › 区画ごとに頼む…. The section rig and the shot echo are always on automatically.
gaps: repeat.same is opt-in and off by default, including for new documents. By default, repeats match only on the camera shot and share layout, motion and decorations only 12–20 % of the time.

No automatic shared 'kit' or family of looks per song part (Aメロ/Bメロ/サビ) for layout, entrance, hold, exit, decorations, lens, screen effects or text face/style. Recency (×0.03 previous, ×0.35 near, ×0.5 same family) actively pushes each cut away from its neighbours.
No per-section mood or amounts: the mood, theme and 強さ are work-level only.

Without '#' headings or an AI song analysis, feat.section is null, so there is no section rig change, no section shot weights and no section background break (blank-line blocks are not used as sections).
サビ1 and サビ2 share a rig row but not a rig choice unless repeat.same is on: each run draws its own rig with the runner-up rule.
survey.designNotes:
Two independent, gated changes.
(1) Make repeats match by default for new documents only. core/doc defaultDoc (or the new-project flow in ui/project_io) writes the pin 'work:repeat.same' = { v: true, by: 'user' }. Existing documents and the v2 fixtures carry no pin, so tests/golden/frame_hashes_v2.json and plan_hashes.json stay byte-identical. alignments() already costs one set lookup without the pin. The toggle UI already exists.
(2) A new opt-in slot 'section.kit', UI name 「パートごとに演出をそろえる」: a work pin, a line pin to exempt lines, never a cut (add it to commands NOT_CUT like repeat.same).
- In planner/cast (or a new planner/kit.js), before casting, compute for each section kind a seeded kit: kitSeed = hash32('kit', look.seed, sectionKind, salts['kit/'+kind]). For each kind (arrange, arrive, dwell, depart, lens, ornament, filter), take 1–2 preferred families drawn by Gumbel over the families in the mood-weighted pool, plus a text.face and a text.style. Key it by section KIND, not instance, so サビ1/サビ2/大サビ share the kit and repeated parts come back alike, and inserting a line changes nothing.
- In choose.preWeight, add a factor 'kit' (e.g. ×4 for a family in the kit; FACTORS.KIT), passed as req.kit from chooseAuto. Recency and the §8.2 avoid stay, so neighbours still differ inside the family.
- Optionally give each section amounts multipliers (verse motion ×0.8, chorus ×1.15), applied only under the pin. Gating amounts also changes pools, so it must go through LK.gateAmounts per section.
- Sections: fall back to planner/areas blocks (blank-line 'para') when feat.section is null.
- Determinism: pure hash seeds. The cast cache (castKeys/castInputs) must include the kit id of the cut's section; feat.section is already in the features id.
- Explain: trace the factor, why code 'section.kit' {section} 「{section}の演出セットに合わせた」, and a whyRule.
- UI: 作品全体 › 見た目 toggle next to 「くり返しの行をそろえる」 (fld.sectionKit, fld.sectionKit.note). On the 区画 page (「n行を選択中」 with an area), a row 「この区画の演出セット」 with a 振り直し die (salt 'kit/<kind>') and the kit's family names.
- Strings: pairs [ja, en] in src/i18n/strings.js (i18n.test.js checks parity).
- Tests: new tests/node/section_kit.test.js: no pin → identical plan hash; on → in-section family concentration well above the song-wide baseline (the m1.js metric); サビ1 and サビ2 share kit families; no identical adjacent arrange/arrive; stability (insert ≤ 4 others, reroll ≤ 3); explain equals plan.
risks: frame_hashes_v2 and plan_hashes break if either change becomes default for existing documents or fixtures. Default-on must be written as a pin into new documents only.

Too much uniformity makes a section look monotonous. The kit factor has to be tuned against recency so the variety tests (≥ 60 % of eligible parts used, neighbour repetition < 1.5 %) still pass on default documents and stay reasonable under the pin.
A kit that is too narrow can empty pools after role, orient, script, season and avoid filters. The fallback must be 'factor 1 when no kit family is in the pool', never a hard filter.
Interaction with repeat.same: the aligned source must still win over the kit. Pins and locks win over both.
Cast cache correctness: a kit reroll salt must invalidate exactly the cuts of that section kind.
The AI direct tool does not know the kit. Area instructions become pins and still win, but the review may need a warning like ai.warn.repeatSame.

verdict.reasoning: I checked every cited symbol and each one exists and does what the report says. cast.js alignments() returns null unless PA.pinned(ctx.ix,'repeat.same'). ui/fields.js has the toggle under PAGES.work sec('look') (offClears, off by default) and the line field repeatLineField (basic:false). camera.js has SHOT_ECHO=40, SHOT_SECTION, RIG_WEIGHTS, rigRow/splitRuns/rigs/rigCopy and LAST_CHORUS_AMP=1.25. choose.js has ECHO=2.5. tracks.js breakScore gives +1 on a section change, and features.js has HEADING_SECTIONS. I re-ran $SCRATCH/survey/m1.js and got the reported numbers exactly: by default, same arrange 15.9 %, arrive 12.0 %, cam.shot 64.3 %, text.face 39.6 %; with the opt-in, 100/99.5/100 %; within-section arrange-family share 22.4 % against 19.5 % song-wide. I also looked for per-part consistency under other names. cast.js never reads feat.section (grep finds nothing), no part's fits reads f.section or sectionStart, and look.js has only work-level mood and amounts. So the repeat half exists as a reachable opt-in that is off by default, and the per-part half exists only for the camera (rig per section, shot weights per section) and for background breaks. Partial is correct. The report missed a manual path and some limits (below). Its default-on design is also wrong in a way the frozen test would not catch.
extraEvidence: Manual path the report missed: 見た目をコピー / 見た目を貼り付け (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V; also in the inspector menu). It is src/ui/boot.js def('look.copy') and pasteLook(), which call src/core/commands.js pinCopy() with copyable() (parts, text.*, motion.speed, cam.*). It copies only the PINS at the source scope, so a line whose look is automatic copies nothing until it is pinned or locked (固定). It is a manual tool, not automatic per-part consistency.

Repeats are exact whole-line text matches only. src/planner/plan.js featureContexts() sets firstOf by line.text, and cast.js alignments() also requires src.text === cut.text, the same role and the same impact. A repeated lyric with one word or one punctuation mark changed, or a phrase repeated inside a longer line, is not a repeat. Under the opt-in, a line sung twice in a row deliberately gets its own look for the first run ('The first run's own copies are chosen').

Typeface class changes cut by cut: cast.js decideText() draws text.face per cut from display/serif/body weighted 3/2(×2 vertical)/1 (FACE_WEIGHTS). Without the opt-in, repeats matched text.face only 39.6 % of the time in m1.js, and nothing keeps the face constant within a section.
camera.decideSpeed() returns a constant auto motion.speed of 1, so no section runs faster or slower.
The whole-song AI tool AI › 区画ごとに頼む… (ai.board.open) can address 'サビ（すべて）' (planner/areas songKind, string area.songAll), but only with an AI song analysis and an AI call. It is not a planner rule.
AI 演出3案 (src/ai/looks.js proposalsRequest) picks arrange/arrive/depart/dwell for 2–6 key lines only, pinned per line. It is AI-only and does not reach every repeat of a line.
correctedGaps: Only exact-text repeats come back alike, and only with 「くり返しの行をそろえる」 on. It is off by default, including for new documents. By default, repeats share layout and motion only 12–23 % of the time; only the camera shot (64 %) and orient/filter.count (about 60 %) match more often.

There is no automatic per-part family ('kit') for layout, entrance, hold, exit, decoration, lens, screen effect, typeface class (text.face is redrawn every cut) or motion speed. The planner (cast.js) never reads feat.section. Only camera rigs and shots, EXTREME shots and background breaks are section-aware.
サビ1 and サビ2 share a rig weight row but not a rig choice unless repeat.same is on.
Without '#' headings or an AI song analysis, feat.section is null, so nothing is section-aware at all. Blank-line blocks (まとまり) are not used by the planner, only by planner/areas after planning.
The manual route (見た目をコピー/貼り付け) copies pins only. To match an automatic look, the user has to pin or lock (固定) first.
verdict.designCorrections:
(1) Default-on for new documents: do NOT put the pin in core/doc defaultDoc(). D.normalize() uses defaultDoc() as the base and fillMissing(doc.pins, base.pins) adds any missing key. core/migrate.parseFile() normalizes every opened file, so the pin would be injected into every existing project and autosave on open and silently change its look. tests/node/frame.test.js plans the raw fixture docs without normalize, so the frozen frame_hashes_v2 test would stay green and never catch it. Instead, add a separate D.newDoc() (defaultDoc plus the new-document settings) and call it only where a new work is created: ui/project_io.js newWork(), the clear-device reset in project_io (loadProject(D.defaultDoc(),…) near line 1176), and boot.js's initial store when no autosave is restored. Add a doc.test.js case: normalize(old doc) never adds pins. Also note that a pin with by:'user' is removed by 作品全体 › 固定を外す (boot 'pin.clearSelection' → commands pinClearUnder('work') drops every non-lock work pin), which would silently turn the default off. Either exempt these setting slots from pinClearUnder, or store the new-document default as a document marker that normalize never fills (for example look.gen, absent = legacy; add it to the cast-cache look key in plan.js stage 5, EN.canon([...])) and keep the pin only for explicit on/off.
(2) Section kit: the reroll salt key 'kit/<kind>' is invalid. core/doc checkSalts and commands.checkSaltKey accept only keys that parse with core/paths.scopeKey (work | line/<id> | cut/<key>, optional :slot). Use a work-scope slot salt such as 'work:kit.chorus' (a NAME_SLOT). castKeys().salts(cut) folds only 'cut/<key>' and 'line/<id>' salts into castInputs, so a work-scope kit salt, the kit pin and the kit id of the cut's section must be added to castInputs explicitly (a new INPUT_FIELDS entry); otherwise cached casts are reused stale after a kit reroll. Do not add a new feat field: encode/Plan bytes would change for every document. Compute the section-kind key in ctx during stage 4, and only when the pin or marker is on. For the no-heading fallback, planner/areas cannot be used, because it indexes a finished (doc, plan). Derive blocks in plan.featureContexts from line.pauseBefore > 0 (core/lyrics makeLine). Give a block a pseudo-kind by matching its first line's text to an earlier block, so repeated chorus blocks share a kit without headings or AI. Apply the kit factor after alignedPart (repeat.same wins) and never as a filter, and keep AVOID_REPEAT and recency. Tests: section_kit.test.js as proposed, plus: normalize/migrate of every fixture adds no pins, and pin.clearUnder('work') behaviour for the new slot.

survey.request: 動きの配分や方向の交互など、文字PVの定石を組み込み
survey.summary: Several conventions are built in and on by default: no identical neighbouring layout or entrance, recency and family damping for every slot, no repeated neighbouring transitions or backgrounds, and song energy (loudness percentile, or a fallback formula without a song) driving which parts fit, their speed and size, zoom and transition frequency. Impact lines get strong parts and snapZoom, section starts open wide, sections weight shots and rigs, and the last chorus rig is bigger. Missing: direction alternation (left/right, in/out) — direction parameters are drawn independently per cut — and a song-level plan for where strong moves go (verse vs chorus, calm after strong).
evidence: src/planner/cast.js AVOID_REPEAT = {arrange, arrive} + avoidOf() + choose.pick avoid runner-up: DESIGN §8.2 'no identical adjacent arrange/arrive' (tests/node/planner_variety.test.js 'no identical adjacent arrange/arrive…', 'neighbour repetition stays under 1.5 %').

src/planner/choose.js RECENT_PREV 0.03, RECENT_NEAR 0.35, SAME_FAMILY 0.5 (withRecency) and src/planner/tracks.js avoidOf(): no neighbour repeats for seams, grounds and atmos (planner_variety 'neighbouring transitions, backgrounds and atmospheres rarely repeat').
src/planner/camera.js SHOT_RECENT 0.2 / SHOT_NEAR 0.5 and autoRig() avoid: shots and section rigs vary between neighbours (camera_planner.test.js 'the moving shots of a video vary…').

src/planner/features.js cutFeatures(): energy = the loudness percentile of the song digest over the cut; without a song, 0.35 + 0.4·repeats + 0.15·impact + 0.1·sin(π·pos), a crude arc that also favours choruses.

src/planner/choose.js traitFit()/rangeFit(): part traits.energy ranges (e.g. arrive stampPress/zoomSettle/skewSlide [0.4,1], inkRise/fogIn [0,0.7–0.8]; depart shardBurst [0.4,1]); weight falls to 0.15 outside the range.

Part params with auto follow 'energy' / '-energy' (e.g. src/parts/arrive/*.js dur range follow '-energy', spread/turn follow 'energy'); src/planner/cast.js decideText(): text.scale = 1 + (energy−0.5)·0.2.

src/planner/camera.js decideCamera(): cam.zoom lerp by energy, cam.curve CURVES_FAST when energy ≥ 0.65, CURVES_IMPACT on impact; baseWeight(): snapZoom 30 on impact, pullReveal 2 on sectionStart, wideHold on long calm cuts; SHOT_SECTION and RIG_WEIGHTS per section; LAST_CHORUS_AMP 1.25 + slowBloom.

src/planner/choose.js IMPACT = 6 (impact cut × part with traits.impact); src/planner/cast.js decideList(): filter.count +1 on impact when amounts.flash > 0; src/planner/tracks.js impulses (flash/shake/slip at every impact cut, punch at song.info.highlights).
src/planner/tracks.js seam chance = mood.pace.seam · (0.5 + 0.5·energy); src/planner/segment.js focus cut chance mood.pace.focus.

Direction params are random per cut: src/parts/seam/wipe.js DIR_PARAM auto pick left/right/up/down weights 3/2/1/1; src/parts/arrive/flip.js dir cw/ccw/alt 2/1/1; src/parts/depart/drift.js dir auto 'left' (fixed); src/parts/arrive/gather.js skewSlide always from the reading side; src/planner/extreme.js mirrorOf(): hash32('xmirror') & 1, with whipPan pairs keeping the SAME direction.

Measured ($SCRATCH/survey/m2b.js, basic/lrc/vertical × 10 seeds × 2 aspects): strong arrive share by energy quartile 20 % / 29 % / 37 % / 40 %; transitions 26 % → 52 %. So energy shapes the distribution only mildly. 6 of 28 consecutive directional seams kept the same direction (independent draws, no alternation rule). $SCRATCH/survey/m2.js basic fixture: verse vs chorus strong-arrive 40 % vs 42 %, moving shots 30 % vs 30 %.

docs/DESIGN.md §4.16.4 (chooser formula), §4.16.6 (no neighbour repeats), §8.2 test table; docs/DESIGN_2_1.md §4.7 (camera weights, rigs); SPEC.md §'Planner … avoids repeating the same choice in neighbouring cuts'.
survey.userPath: Automatic in おまかせ planning. The user steers it through 作品全体 › 強さ (動き, カットの速さ, カメラワーク, 見せ場で光る, 揺れ …), through 行 › 文字の記号 › 見せ場（!） and 強調 on lines, and through '#' headings or 曲の分析 (AI) for sections. No 定石 switch or rule list exists in the UI.
gaps: No direction alternation: entrance, exit and transition directions (left/right/up/down), rotation direction, EXTREME mirror and camera push-in/pull-out are drawn independently per cut. Nothing makes the next cut go the opposite way, or zoom out after a zoom in.

No song-level motion budget or energy arc. Nothing reserves the strongest moves for choruses, sectionStart or the last chorus (beyond the rig amp ×1.25). Nothing keeps verses calmer when the audio energy is flat, and there is no 'calm after strong' rhythm between neighbours.
Without audio, energy comes from a fixed formula (repeats, impact, sin(pos)). Section kinds (verse/chorus) are not used for motion strength, only for camera shots and rigs.
No explicit, user-visible list of the 定石 rules and no switch for them. Their effect is mild: in the measured fixture, chorus and verse have about the same share of strong entrances.
survey.designNotes:
Add the conventions behind one gated work switch: slot 'rules.pv', UI name 「文字PVの定石」. It is off for existing documents (frame_hashes_v2 / plan_hashes unchanged) and written as a pin into new documents by core/doc defaultDoc, or offered as a toggle in 作品全体 › 強さ.
(a) Direction alternation.
- Give direction-bearing ParamSpecs a semantic tag (e.g. spec.dir: 'h' | 'v' | 'rot' with opposite pairs) in the kit: seam wipe dir, depart drift dir, flip dir, and a new side param for skewSlide. Also classify shot presets as in or out (pushWord/snapZoom/readAlong = in; pullReveal/driftOff/wideHold = out) in core/shot.
- In planner/params resolveParams (through ax, lookAx) or in cast.decidePart after resolveParams, pick the opposite of the previous cut's direction with probability p (e.g. 0.75) under the switch, from the param's own stream.
- In camera.weighShots add a factor ×1.5 for the opposite in/out class and ×0.6 for the same.
- To keep locality (the NOTES discussion of chaining in tracks avoidOf), read the previous cut's NATURAL pick (hist rows 'own'/base), not its final value, so a change does not propagate down the song.
(b) Motion budget and arc.
- Compute a per-cut 'drive' in planner/plan stage 4 from section kind and position: verse 0.35, prechorus rising, chorus 0.75, last chorus 0.9, bridge contrast. Blend it with feat.energy only under the switch; to keep Plan bytes identical when off, add no new feat field unless gated.
- Use it in traitFit energy and in a new chooser factor that damps fast/hard/bold-tagged parts after a strong neighbour ('calm after strong', ×0.6 against the previous cut's natural pick).
- Reserve traits.impact parts and snapZoom-like moves for impact, sectionStart and chorus cuts.
- Why codes: 'pv.alternate' 「前のカットと逆向きにした」, 'pv.arc' 「サビに向けて強い動きを取っておいた」, 'pv.calm' 「強い動きの後なので落ち着かせた」.
- UI: 作品全体 › 強さ, a toggle 「文字PVの定石」 with a note listing the rules (fld.pvRules, fld.pvRules.note).
- Tests: new tests/node/pv_rules.test.js: off → identical plan hash; on → alternation rate of consecutive directional params ≥ 70 % (the m2b.js metric); strong-part share chorus > verse by a margin with and without audio; planner_stability insert/reroll bounds still hold; planner_explain equals plan; planner_determinism.
risks: Byte-identity: any change to default param autos or chooser factors for existing documents changes frames (frame_hashes_v2) and plan hashes, so everything must sit behind a pin that only new documents get.

Locality and stability: alternation that reads the previous cut's final value chains changes down the song. The reroll ≤ 3 and insert ≤ 4 bounds of planner_stability, and the echo/twin machinery in cast.createHistory, make this delicate. Base it on natural picks and extend ROW_FIELDS/TWIN_FIELDS if new row fields are read.
Repeated lines: under repeat.same a copy takes its source's params (copyParams). Alternation must not override aligned params, and the echo should keep the first copy's direction.
A strong arc can make verses dull or fight the mood (dashSprint should stay lively). Tune against catalog.test.js mood-distinction tests.
Parts that encode direction internally (skewSlide reading-side rule for vertical text) must not be flipped where that breaks readability.

verdict.reasoning: The cited default-on conventions are real and on by default. They are AVOID_REPEAT in cast.js with choose.pick's avoid runner-up, RECENT_PREV 0.03 / RECENT_NEAR 0.35 / SAME_FAMILY 0.5, energy traitFit, IMPACT ×6, snapZoom 30 on impact, pullReveal on sectionStart, SHOT_SECTION/RIG_WEIGHTS, LAST_CHORUS_AMP, and a seam chance that scales with energy. Direction alternation does not exist anywhere. grep for alternat/opposite/交互 finds only intra-part effects (flip 'alt', gather's alternating sides, diptych). Every direction-bearing parameter is an independent per-cut auto. It is worse than reported: the normal camera presets have one fixed direction and cannot be mirrored at all. There is no song-level motion budget. motion.speed is a constant 1, and cast.js never reads feat.section. The only written '定石' in the codebase is AI prompt text for EXTREME mode (ai/direct.js SYSTEM_CAMERA_XMODE), which needs AI and is opt-in. Partial stands. The report's locality suggestion for alternation is logically wrong (below).
extraEvidence: Normal camera shots have a fixed direction and no mirror. core/shot.js SHOTS: sweepAcross keys ox −0.12 → +0.12 (always left to right), driftOff ox +0.18, tiltHold roll −4/−2. Rigs: driftSide x −0.02 → +0.02, leanTilt roll +2.5. The '~m' mirror (core/shot xKeyOf/mirrorKeys, SHOT.MIRRORS = dutchSwing/orbit/spinIn/spinOut/whipPan) exists only for EXTREME presets. With the camera alone, consecutive sweeps and drifts can only go the same way.

More independent direction autos the report did not list: src/parts/lens/glide.js pan dir right/left/down/up 3/3/1/1 and rotate dir cw/ccw. Composition side and corner: arrange/columns.js side left/right 3/2 and align right/center, arrange/core.js corner bottomLeft/… 4/3/2/1 and echo dir down/up/split 4/1/1, arrange/special.js corner, arrange/editorial.js band upper/middle/lower. Also ornament/digital.js corner and filter/glow.js side. Left/right placement across cuts does not alternate either.

camera.js decideSpeed(): the auto motion.speed is always 1. Only part params (dur follow '-energy', spread/turn follow 'energy') and text.scale 1+(energy−0.5)·0.2 react to energy. No section-based speed.

No part fits and no cast.js code reads feat.section or feat.sectionStart (grep finds nothing in src/parts and cast.js). Section kinds shape only camera shots (SHOT_SECTION), rigs (RIG_WEIGHTS), EXTREME weights (extreme.js SECTION) and background breaks.

The only text-motion vs camera exclusions are per layout: arrange cam:'none' (edgeBleed, diptych, strip, pattern) and cam:'gentle' (shotRules), plus a framing lens raising 'none' +24. A fast/hard arrive and a snapZoom or whip can coincide freely.

ai/direct.js SYSTEM_CAMERA_XMODE is the only written convention ('strongest moves on impact lines, the chorus …; lighter extreme moves in verses …; do not give the same extreme move to more than two lines in a row'). It needs AI and カメラ EXTREME. SYSTEM_CAMERA_MODE similarly asks for calm shots in quiet parts. Both are AI-only.

History rows (cast.js historyRow) store only slot values (part keys) in base/both/last/own, never params. decidePart resolves params only when !st.natural, so the natural pass has no directions at all.

tests/node/planner_stability.test.js compare() checks only the part keys in SLOTS (orient, arrange, arrive, dwell, depart, lens, ornament#i, filter#i), not params. A chain of flipped directions would pass every existing stability bound unnoticed.
correctedGaps: No direction alternation of any kind. Entrance, exit, transition (wipe dir), lens pan and rotation (glide dir), composition side and corner, and EXTREME mirror are drawn independently per cut. The normal camera presets and rigs have a single fixed direction and cannot be mirrored, so camera direction cannot alternate even by chance.
No push-in / pull-out alternation between neighbouring shots. SHOT_RECENT (×0.2) only discourages the same preset.

No song-level motion budget or arc. Strength follows the per-cut energy percentile (mildly: strong entrances 20 % → 40 % across energy quartiles) but not the section kind. motion.speed is constant. Nothing reserves the strongest moves for the chorus, sectionStart or the last chorus (apart from the rig amp ×1.25 and slowBloom), and nothing calms the cut after a strong one.
Without audio, energy is 0.35 + 0.4·(line sung more than once) + 0.15·impact + 0.1·sin(π·pos), so any repeated line, not only choruses, counts as high energy.
The only explicit 定石 text is in the AI prompts for EXTREME mode. There is no switch or rule list for users, and nothing that works without AI.
verdict.designCorrections:
(1) Gating: same flaw as M1. 'written as a pin into new documents by core/doc defaultDoc' would leak into every opened project, because D.normalize fills missing pins from defaultDoc() and migrate.parseFile calls it. The frozen frame test plans raw fixtures and would not catch this. Use a D.newDoc() at the new-work call sites (project_io newWork, the clear-device reset, boot's initial doc), or a non-normalized document marker. Remember that 作品全体 › 固定を外す (pinClearUnder('work')) deletes user work pins.
(2) The report's locality trick for alternation defeats alternation. If cut i takes the opposite of cut i−1's NATURAL draw, the finals of i−1 and i are opposite(n(i−2)) and opposite(n(i−1)), which differ only when n(i−2) ≠ n(i−1), about 50 % for a binary direction. That is no better than today. True alternation must read the previous cut's FINAL direction, so it chains. Bound the chain by restarting the alternation at every rig run or background segment boundary (both are already local: splitRuns, and the memoryless breakScore coin) and at sectionStart. Draw the first cut of a run from its own param stream. Add a param-level stability metric, because planner_stability compare() ignores params.
(3) Directions are not in history rows and the natural pass resolves no params. Add a per-axis direction record to historyRow (e.g. row.dir.h / row.dir.v / row.dir.rot from the final values), add it to ROW_FIELDS for the previous row (and TWIN_FIELDS, twinOf) so castInputs/sameRows invalidate the cast cache, and apply the flip in decidePart after PA.resolveParams, before copyParams (aligned params must win). Seams are decided in tracks (decideSeam, whose result is cached on B's cast entry). The previous seam's dir must enter that cache key.
(4) Camera: add mirrorable normal presets ('sweepAcross~m', 'driftOff~m', 'tiltHold~m', 'driftSide~m', 'leanTilt~m') by extending core/shot's ShotRef coerce/presetOf/mirrorKeys beyond XSHOTS. These are new values only, so old frames are unchanged. Then weighShots can prefer the mirror of the previous shot, and an in/out class factor can apply. Explain (planner/explain ALT_SLOTS) and shot widgets must list the mirrored values.
(5) Arc: compute 'drive' in ctx (not as a new feat field, which changes Plan bytes and plan_hashes) and only under the switch. Also feed it into motion.speed (decideSpeed auto: verse 0.9, chorus 1.1) and into the seam chance. The no-audio fallback should weight section kind, not 'repeated line'.
(6) Tests: pv_rules.test.js as proposed, plus: off → byte-identical plan for every corpus and fixture doc after normalize(); on → alternation rate of consecutive directional params ≥ 70 % within runs; param-level insert/reroll stability bounded by run length; mirrored shot values round-trip through core/shot coerce.

survey.summary: Only caps inside each kind and a few pairwise rules exist: up to 3 decorations, up to 2 automatic screen effects (+1 on impact lines), no repeating the whole-video texture as an effect, no camera shot on some layouts or under a framing lens, and a few compatibility factors. engine/scene/budget.js is a glyph-cover and performance budget for user materials only, not an effect cap. There is no limit on how many effect layers stack on one cut: measured means are 2.8–3.9 layers per lyric cut with a maximum of 7, and about 5 on impact lines plus flash, shake and slip impulses together.
evidence: src/planner/cast.js LIST_MAX = 3, SLOT_SPECS 'ornament.count'/'filter.count' int 0–3; decideList(): ornament.count = min(3, floor(amounts.ornament·2.5 + r)); filter.count = min(2, floor(0.8·filterDrive + r)) + (impact && amounts.flash > 0 ? 1 : 0); a pin on slot i raises the count (rule 'index').

src/planner/cast.js poolEntry(): the work texture leaves every filter#i pool ('no texture repeated as an effect', NOTES 'Moods look like their names': 47 → 0 doubled textures); ownValues(): no two equal decorations or effects in one cut (recency 'own').

src/planner/camera.js shotRules(): arrange cam:'none' forces shot none, cam:'gentle' limits the pool and caps zoom (0.7/maxFill); baseWeight(): 'none' + 24 when the lens frames (lens def.frames), so a framing lens rarely also gets a camera move; AMOUNT_OFF/RIG_OFF gates.

Pairwise fits: src/parts/dwell/lively.js fits ×0 on BOUND arranges; src/parts/filter/frame.js fits ×0.1 on EDGE_HUGGERS arranges; src/parts/filter/flash.js and src/parts/lens/kick.js fits 0.25 off-impact.

src/core/recipe LIMITS (DESIGN_2_1 §5.8): per-material caps (layers, particles, filter stack Σcost ≤ 6, flash rule). Materials only.
src/planner/tracks.js impulses: every impact cut gets flash (amounts.flash), shake (amounts.shake) and slip (amounts.glitch > 0.2) at the same t, in addition to the cut's parts.
tests/node/catalog.test.js 'film moods show their screen effects, and a cut never repeats the work texture as one'; tests/node/budget.test.js (glyph budget); no test bounds the total effects per cut.

Measured ($SCRATCH/survey/t5.js; basic+long × 3 seeds × 2 aspects × 8 moods; layers = ornament.count + filter.count + non-fixedFrame lens + moving cam.shot + non-hardCut transition into the cut). Mean per lyric cut: quietHush 2.83 (max 5), popFizz 3.91 (max 7), dashSprint/glitchFracture 3.81 (max 7). Impact cuts: 4.4–5.1 on average for the lively moods, max 7, not counting the impulses.
survey.userPath: No dedicated control. Indirectly: 作品全体 › 強さ (装飾の量, 乱れ, 色ずれ, 質感, 見せ場で光る, 揺れ, カメラワーク) lowers amounts for the whole video. Per cut: 要素 › 装飾 / 画面効果 › 数 can be pinned to 0–3, and parts can be pinned or excluded (作品全体 › 部品, 行 › この行で使わない部品).
gaps: No cross-kind cap per cut (decorations + screen effects + lens movement + camera shot + transition + impulses). Kinds are decided independently; only ornament and filter each have their own count cap.

Impact lines stack the most: filter +1, IMPACT ×6 parts (edgeBleed, stampPress, shardBurst, impactKick, flashPop/invertBlink), snapZoom weight 30, and flash, shake and slip impulses all at the same time.
No mood-aware limit (e.g. calm moods ≤ 2 layers) and no user setting 「1カットの効果は○つまで」 or 「効果を重ねすぎない」.

survey.designNotes:
Add a per-cut effect load cap in planner/cast behind a gated switch.
- Slot 'fx.cap' (int 0–6, or bool) at work or line scope, UI 「効果を重ねすぎない」. Off (no pin) for existing documents and written as a pin into new documents by defaultDoc, so frame_hashes_v2 and plan_hashes stay byte-identical.
- The FROZEN slot order already helps: ornament.count → ornament#i → lens → cam.* → filter.count → filter#i.
- Compute load = ornament.count + (lens not still, i.e. not fixedFrame/'still' family) + (moving cam.shot) + (strong arrive/depart by tags fast/hard/bold or traits.impact) + (impact cut ? 1 : 0).
- At filter.count, clamp the auto count to max(0, cap − load) with from 'rule' and rule 'fx.cap'. Earlier, at ornament.count, clamp against a cap that reads the chosen arrange (busy tag) and arrive.
- Only automatic values are reduced; pins and locks win and may exceed the cap (a warning is optional).
- Default caps by mood: pace/amounts, e.g. cap = 3 + round(2·amounts.pace), calm moods ≈ 3–4, lively ≈ 5.
- Transitions: in tracks, lower the text-seam chance when the receiving cut is already at the cap.
- Impulses: on impact cuts under the cap keep at most two of flash/shake/slip, keyed deterministically by hash.
- The camera already avoids stacking with framing lenses. Extend with a factor ×0.3 for moving shots when lens is 'shake'/'beat' family under the switch.
- Explain: why 'fx.cap' 「効果が重なりすぎないように数を減らした」 via decideValue's rule/why. The inspector shows filter.count/ornament.count as rule-reduced.
- Strings in src/i18n/strings.js (fld.fxCap, fld.fxCap.note, why.fx.cap, whyRule.fx.cap).
- Tests: new tests/node/fx_cap.test.js: off → identical plan hash on corpus; on → max load ≤ cap for every mood and impact cut (the t5.js metric) except where pinned; pins honoured (planner_pins fuzz); planner_explain equals plan; film moods still show their effects (catalog.test.js thresholds may need an 'under cap' variant); stability (the cap reads only the same cut's decisions, so it stays local).
risks: Mood identity: glitchFracture, popFizz and dashSprint get their look from stacked effects. A cap that is too low flattens them and can fail catalog.test.js mood-distinction and 'film moods show their screen effects' thresholds if it ever applies by default.
Byte-identity: reducing counts on existing documents changes frames (frame_hashes_v2), so the cap must be gated by a pin that only new documents get.

Order constraints: ornament.count is decided before lens and camera (FROZEN order), so a single global cap can only trim the later slots (filters), or needs a conservative estimate at ornament time. Changing the order is not allowed.
Impulses live in tracks (stage 6). Capping them needs care for determinism and for the export flash-rate preflight.
repeat.same copies take the source's counts (ALIGN_VALUES includes ornament.count and filter.count). The cap must apply consistently to source and copy, or aligned copies may violate or change it.

verdict.reasoning: The caps and pair rules are verified. LIST_MAX 3 and decideList(): ornament min(3, ⌊2.5·ornament + r⌋), filter min(2, ⌊0.8·filterDrive + r⌋) + 1 on impact with flash. The texture is excluded from the filter pools (poolEntry), and ownValues prevents duplicates. shotRules has cam:'none'/'gentle', and a framing lens adds +24 to 'none'. The fits rules exist (lively ×0 on BOUND, frame ×0.1 on EDGE_HUGGERS, flash and kick 0.25 off-impact). budget.js is material-only, and tracks.impulses fires flash/shake/slip on every impact cut. I re-ran $SCRATCH/survey/t5.js and got the same numbers (quietHush mean 2.83, max 5; popFizz 3.91, max 7; impact cuts up to 5.11 on average). No cross-kind cap exists under any name (clutter, budget, load, cap). The metric even undercounts, because it omits the work texture, atmos particles, the section rig and impulses. The owner lists this item under 【文字組み】, so it may mean effects stacked on the lettering itself. That is also only partly handled: text.style is one exclusive value per cut, and draw.js takes max() for a glow style and a motion glow, but motion-part glyph effects and screen effects can still pile onto the text. Partial is right.
extraEvidence: Glyph level (the 文字組み reading): core/registry TEXT_STYLES = plain/outline/shadow/glow/duo. text.style is a single value per cut, taken from the theme (cast.js decideText), so the lettering never stacks two styles. src/engine/render/draw.js (around line 338): 'const halo = rec.style === 'glow' && glow < STYLE_GLOW ? STYLE_GLOW : glow' takes the max of the glow style and a motion glow instead of adding them. Nothing else limits the glyph channels (tint/echo/glow/blur/shard/pixel/grow, engine/scene/behave MASK_GROUPS) that arrive/dwell/depart add on top of text.style and of screen effects that also hit the text (chroma shift, glow spill). The LADDER masks in engine/scene/budget.js apply only to materials (def.mine).

Built-in exclusion on impact cuts: the impact layout edgeBleed (arrange/core.js, traits.impact, ×6 on '!' lines) has cam:'none', so when it wins, the snapZoom (weight 30) is forced off. The two impact boosts compete instead of stacking.

camera.js weighShots reads only lens.frames. Moving lenses (lens/kick.js beat and impact kicks, lens/glide.js pans and rotations) do not lower the weight of moving shots, so a moving lens and a camera move can stack.

A temporal limit exists for flashes only: export/schedule.js preflight 'flash-rate' (FLASH_LIMIT 3 flashes in any 1 s window; fix pins work:amount.flash 0.3; string exp.pre.flash-rate 「1秒間に{n}回の点滅があります」). It is a warning at export time, not a per-cut layer cap.

Several layers are decided after casting, in plan.js stage 6: TR.grounds → TR.seams (with rule overrides that replace neighbouring motions) → XT.shots (the EXTREME overlay replaces cam.shot) → CAM.carry → CAM.rigs → TR.impulses. filter.count, decided at cast time, cannot see any of them.

Under repeat.same, decideValue takes alignedValue (the source's ornament.count/filter.count, ALIGN_VALUES) before autoFn, so a cap written inside the count's autoFn would be bypassed for aligned copies.

The t5.js metric omits the work texture (look.plan.texture, a filter over the whole video), the run-scope atmos particle ornament, the section rig and the flash/shake/slip/punch impulses, so real stacking is higher than 2.8–3.9.
correctedGaps: No cross-kind limit per cut (decorations + screen effects + moving lens + camera shot + section rig + transition + impulses). Only ornament and filter each have their own count cap.

No limit on effects that land on the lettering itself beyond one text.style and max() for glow. Glyph channels from arrive/dwell/depart (tint/echo/glow/blur/shard/pixel/grow) and text-affecting screen effects (chroma shift, glow spill) can pile onto a styled text. The glyph budget masks exist only for materials.
Impact lines stack the most: filter.count +1, parts with traits.impact ×6, snapZoom 30 (unless edgeBleed wins and forces no shot), and flash + shake + slip impulses at the same t.
A moving lens does not discourage a moving camera shot (only framing lenses do).
No mood-aware ceiling and no user setting such as 「効果を重ねすぎない」 or 「1カットの効果は○つまで」. The only related limit is the flash-rate warning at export.
verdict.designCorrections:
(1) Gating: same flaw as M1 and M2. 'written as a pin into new documents by defaultDoc' would reach every opened project through D.normalize (fillMissing on pins) in migrate.parseFile. Use D.newDoc() at the new-work call sites or a marker that normalize does not fill, and note that 作品全体 › 固定を外す (pinClearUnder('work')) deletes user work pins.
(2) A cast-time cap alone cannot be complete. At decideList('filter') the cut knows its own arrange/arrive/ornaments/lens/normal cam.shot, but not the transition into it, an EXTREME shot, carry, the rig or impulses (all in plan stage 6). Split the cap: (a) in cast, trim the automatic filter.count and, at ornament.count, use a conservative estimate from arrange/arrive (decided earlier in the FROZEN order). (b) In tracks.seams, lower the text-seam chance for a receiving cut at the cap; B's slots are in its cast entry, so the seam cache stays correct. (c) In tracks.impulses, keep at most N of flash/shake/slip on an over-cap impact cut, chosen by hash32 of the cut key (deterministic and local). (d) XT.shots only runs under the explicit EXTREME switch; treat that switch as exempt, or have its rules read the cap.
(3) Apply the cap AFTER alignment: decideValue returns alignedValue before autoFn. Either pass an applies() check to alignedValue that rejects a source count over this cut's cap, or clamp after the decision, and make the explain trace say rule 'fx.cap'.
(4) For the 文字組み reading, add a glyph-effect rule under the same switch. Weigh arrive/dwell/depart parts whose glyph channels overlap text.style ×0.3 (glow style against glow-using holds; outline/duo against echo/tint), and do the same for text-hitting filters when the cut already carries a glyph effect. This needs a declared channel list per part (e.g. traits.glyph: ['glow','echo'] checked in core/registry), or it can be derived once from behave's column use. Do not reuse budget.js masks for catalog parts by default, because that changes v2 frames. Only the gated path may.
(5) In weighShots, add a moving-lens factor for kick/glide lenses (e.g. moving shots ×0.4), only under the switch.
(6) Tests: fx_cap.test.js as proposed, but measure load including texture, atmos, rig, seam and impulses. Off → byte-identical plans for all corpus docs after normalize(). On → per-cut load ≤ cap except pinned or locked cuts. Aligned copies respect the cap. The flash-rate preflight count never rises. catalog.test.js mood thresholds are checked with the switch on.

survey.summary: Nothing tightens kana. Every run gets one uniform `tracking` (0 by default), and advances come from Canvas measureText at full width, so each kana takes a full 1 em (the probe confirms 100/100). Canvas2D has no way to turn on palt, and no setting or string anywhere offers kana tightening.
evidence: src/engine/text/layout.js DEFAULTS (l.9): tracking 0. trackedWidth (l.197) and place() add the same `tracking` after every cell, with no per-class adjustment.

src/engine/text/layout.js naturalAdvances (l.154) takes prefix widths from measurer.width, i.e. canvas measureText with default features. src/engine/host/measure.js createCanvasMeasurer never sets letterSpacing, fontKerning or feature settings.
src/engine/text/layout.js alongAdvance (l.180): in vertical text every upright cell (kana included) advances exactly 1 em, so there is no vpal-like tightening either.
docs/DESIGN.md §4.15.5 (l.1386): 'CJK punctuation is not compressed in v2.0'. §4.15.1 Measurer is FROZEN (width, metrics only).

Only per-run uniform tracking exists, and only in a few parts: columns.js numberRun tracking -0.02 (the sidebarIndex number); special.js titlePlate param `spacing` 「名前の字間」 0.12–0.3 em, which widens; scatter.js haloRing/gridMosaic set tracking to hit a grid pitch; dwell creepTrack 「にじり」 animates spacing wider. None of these is kana-aware.
Probe $SCRATCH/survey/t_layout.js (fakeMeasurer, '君のことがLoveなんだ' at size 100): kana x = 50,150,250,350,450, all w 100. No tightening.
No i18n key for 字間/詰め at work, line or cut scope in src/i18n/strings.js. No tracking field in src/ui/fields.js PAGES.
gaps: Kana (hira/kata/smallKana, and ー・ etc.) are not tightened, horizontally or vertically
No palt-like proportional kana (Canvas cannot enable OpenType palt)
No 約物詰め (、。「」 half-width), which DESIGN says is not done in v2.0
No UI setting at 作品全体, 行 or カット
survey.designNotes: Gate it as an opt-in slot so frame_hashes_v2 stays byte-identical. Add a non-part slot in planner/cast.js SLOT_SPECS, e.g. 'text.kana' (bool) or one enum 'text.kumi' shared with T2/T3. Emit it into cut.slots only when pinned (as with 'repeat.same'), so documents without the pin keep the same plan and frames. To turn it on for new projects only, core/doc.js defaultDoc() can seed pins {'work:text.kana': …}; goldens load tests/fixtures/project_*.json, so they are unaffected. Plumbing: engine/scene/build.js buildCutWith passes valueOf(slots,'text.kana') into createBuilder defaults. builder.normalizeRun copies it into the RunSpec unless the part set its own `tracking` (gridMosaic, haloRing, sidebarIndex number and titlePlate name need exact pitch and would opt out). Add the field to engine/text/service.js LAYOUT_FIELDS, or the LRU returns stale layouts. layout.normalizeSpec and prepare(): after naturalAdvances, multiply along[i] for u.cls hira/kata/smallKana (and ー, and optionally 、。「」 as 約物詰め) by a deterministic per-class factor, e.g. kana 0.88–0.92 and small kana 0.75. Trim symmetrically so the glyph centre `at = pen + adv/2` stays centred. Apply the same factor to vertical upright kana in alongAdvance. trackedWidth, greedy/balance and fitsAt all read `along`, so breaking and fitting stay consistent automatically. A more faithful option: add an optional, additive Measurer.ink(css, g) (canvas actualBoundingBoxLeft/Right; a class table in fake_measure) and derive the trim from the side bearings, falling back to the table when it is missing (Measurer is FROZEN, so additive only). Arrange sizing (bestFit on S.cells) can stay; text only ends slightly narrower. UI: 作品全体 › 書体 gets a toggle 「かなを詰める」 with a note. Overrides go in 行 › 色と書体 and カット › 構図 next to 文字の大きさ. Strings are [ja, en] pairs in i18n/strings.js. Tests: layout.test.js (width shrinks by the expected em with fakeMeasurer; field absent gives RunLayout arrays identical to today), a service cache-key test, vertical.test.js, update_golden.js --check (frame_hashes_v2 must match), and a new golden fixture like project_repeat.json with the pin on. Check the look visually with contact sheets / glyph_parity.
risks: Canvas2D cannot enable palt/vpal, so any tightening is an approximation. A fixed table can make neighbours touch in heavy or brush faces (Dela Gothic One, Yuji Syuku). An ink-bbox approach depends on the real font and its load state (measurer key/epoch already invalidates caches).
Cells narrower than the ink: pick boxes, inkBox, reveal wipes and per-glyph motions read cell w and may clip or overlap slightly.
Parts that need exact pitch (gridMosaic, haloRing, tracking-based runs) must opt out or their grids misalign.
Changing the default for existing documents breaks frame_hashes_v2. It must stay opt-in or new-documents-only, and the slot must not appear in plans without a pin, or plan_hashes changes too.
If the field is missing from LAYOUT_FIELDS, the service cache serves layouts without tightening after the toggle changes.

verdict.reasoning: Status confirmed. survey.request: 文字が溶けて変わる、同じ字が移動するモーフ
survey.summary: The 'melt into the next text' half exists as an image-level transition: the seam blendDissolve 溶け合い (plus the ink mask sumiSeep 墨にじみ). It is picked automatically at about 12% of boundaries and can be pinned. There is no per-glyph morph and no magic move of shared characters: seams only see two composited surfaces, with no glyph identity.
evidence: src/parts/seam/soft.js blendDissolve 「溶け合い」 (scope 'text', traits energy [0, 0.75]): the old words blur (soften up to 1.6x) and fade over u in [0, 0.7] while the new words firm up over [0.2, 0.8]. Blurb: 前の文字がぼやけながら次の文字へ溶けていく. sumiSeep 「墨にじみ」: the new words bleed in through spreading ink blots.

src/engine/render/seam.js mix(ctl, pool, part, a, b, u) and src/engine/render/renderer.js drawTextSeam: a text seam receives only A's and B's text/near layers as two pooled surfaces. DESIGN.md §4.19.2 step 4 and the §4.18 catalog contract define a seam as `mix(fx, a, b, u, p)` with scope 'text' or 'world'. No glyph list reaches a seam.

src/planner/tracks.js seams(): inside a background segment, a text seam is chosen with probability mood.pace.seam*(0.5+0.5*energy). Across segments, a world seam is chosen 70% of the time. Window: [B.a - dur/2, B.a + dur/2], clamped to 0.4 x the shorter cut.

Measured with $SCRATCH/survey/m4_seams.js (SAMPLE_JA, 8 moods x 2 aspects x 4 seeds, 3136 boundaries): sumiSeep 13.5%, blendDissolve 12.4%, world seams 0.8-3% each. In one plan, 11 of 49 consecutive cut pairs share at least one character.

A grep for morph / magic / shared glyph / same glyph finds nothing in src or docs. src/planner/camera.js carry (§4.5.7) is a camera match cut between phrases of the same line (B opens at A's closeness, screen position and roll). It keeps the framing continuous but does not move glyphs.

Glyph draw records carry rec.ch / rec.font / rec.em / rec.style (src/engine/render/draw.js), and scene tables hold world matrices (table.m) and world alpha (table.wa). A renderer-level grapheme matcher would therefore have the data it needs.

Tests: lens_filter_seam.test.js 'blendDissolve: the old words melt away before the new ones firm up'; its line 125 asserts the text-scope auto pool is [blendDissolve, hardCut, sumiSeep]; facade.test.js 'a text seam mixes the two text layers…'.
arrive shardGather / ghostConverge (arrive/gather.js) assemble a glyph from fragments or ghost copies of the same glyph. Nothing comes from the previous line's glyphs.
survey.userPath: 自動：同じ背景の中のカット切り替えで「溶け合い」が約12%の確率で選ばれる。手動：③ 見た目 → カット →「切り替え」で「溶け合い」（または「墨にじみ」）を選ぶ／行 → 演出（すべてのカット）→「切り替え（行の始まり）」で選ぶ。
gaps: No per-glyph morph where each character dissolves into the character that takes its place. The dissolve works on the whole image, so both lines blur and fade as blocks.
No magic move: characters shared by consecutive lines (e.g. 君が好き → 君が嫌い, or repeated words) do not travel from their old position, size and rotation to their new ones.
The seam API gets no glyph data (mix(fx, a, b, u, p) receives only surfaces), and the planner knows nothing about text shared between consecutive cuts.
The seam window is clamped to 0.4 x the shorter cut, which may be too short for a readable move on fast lyrics.
survey.designNotes: Add a new seam part, e.g. `glyphMorph` 「文字モーフ」, with a new scope 'glyph' (additive, next to 'text' and 'world'). It uses the existing replace rule `replaces: { depart: true, arrive: true }`, so A's exit becomes instantHide and B's entrance becomes instantShow and they do not fight the move. The contract needs a new call such as `morph(gx, A, B, u, p)`, where A and B are glyph lists { ch, font, em, ink, style, screenMatrix, alpha }. This needs a DESIGN addendum to §4.18 / §4.19.2; the existing scopes stay frozen as they are. Engine (src/engine/render/renderer.js, a new branch beside drawTextSeam): after behaviours and world transforms are solved for both scenes, collect the glyph nodes of A's last cut and B's first cut and compute their screen matrices (view(cam, text layer)·m). Screen space is required because A and B may have different cameras. Match graphemes by LCS in reading order, breaking ties deterministically by nearest position and then by index. Draw each matched pair once, with the 2x3 matrix decomposed into translate/scale/rotate and interpolated through the seam curve (CV.warp), and ink/style crossfaded. Unmatched A glyphs dissolve out (alpha plus blur, as blendDissolve does) and unmatched B glyphs dissolve in. Non-glyph nodes (plates, near-layer ornaments) crossfade. Planner: register it with pool:false (pin-only, like photoPan). Existing auto picks then stay unchanged, frame_hashes_v2 stays byte-identical, and the pool list in lens_filter_seam.test.js holds. Later, a work opt-in (作品全体 → 演出, e.g. 「同じ字をつなぐ」, modeled on work:repeat.same) could let tracks.js seams() pick it (rule 'morph', why text) on boundaries where the cuts share at least N graphemes, computed only when opted in so existing fingerprints do not change. It may also want a longer window than 0.4 x the cut. UI: the part browser already lists pool:false parts for pinning (カット → 切り替え, 行 → 切り替え（行の始まり）). Labels come from the part's L(ja, en), and a DESIGN catalog table row is needed because the docs tests read those tables. Tests: node tests with the recording context (src/engine/render/record.js) showing that u=0 draws exactly A, u=1 draws exactly B, and each matched glyph is drawn once; determinism; pick.js during the window; frame goldens unchanged without the pin; a browser lab/contact sheet for visual QA.
risks: Correspondence is ambiguous for repeated kana or kanji (「のの」) and when glyph counts differ, so wrong pairings may cross the screen.
Different faces, sizes or orientations between cuts (h vs v, rotated Latin in vertical text, tate-chu-yoko cells, emphasis scale) can make the interpolation look odd.
A and B may have different cameras or shots, so the move must happen in screen space. The ground camera blend in text seams must stay consistent with it.
The FROZEN glyph path rule (§4.19.5: direct vs sprite chosen only from pose) and export/preview parity must still hold at intermediate scales. Sprite quality and cache growth at in-between sizes.
The extra per-glyph work during seam windows must stay within the preview frame budget.
Making it an auto pick without an opt-in would change existing plans and break frame_hashes_v2.

verdict.reasoning:
The cited evidence checks out. seam/soft.js blendDissolve 溶け合い is blurbed 前の文字がぼやけながら次の文字へ溶けていく, which covers the first half of the request (文字が溶けて変わる) at image level. I searched for morph, tween, magic, carry, swap, scramble, shared or same glyph. There is no glyph-level correspondence anywhere. camera.js carry (§4.5.7) is a camera match cut only.

One more near miss: depart meltDown「溶け」(depart/fall.js:236) melts the glyphs downward, but it does not become the next text.

The 'same characters move' half is entirely missing. The 'melt into the next text' half exists only as a whole-image crossfade. Partial stands, with the core glyph-level morph missing.
extraEvidence: depart meltDown「溶け」(src/parts/depart/fall.js:236-238): 文字が下へ垂れて伸び、にじみながら消える. A melting exit on A that knows nothing about B.

B's own entrance motion plays inside the dissolve (seam/soft.js notes that b's entrance begins at u=0.5), so the new text does its own entrance while the old one melts: two motions, not one transformation. tracks.js seams() supports replaces.arrive (l.559, replaceMotion to instantShow; DESIGN.md l.1535-1536), but none of today's 8 replacing seams use it. All replace only depart, so the arrive branch has never run in practice.

Seam materials exist. ai/recipe.js builds マイ素材 seams from a base part (tests/node/ai_recipe.test.js uses base 'blendDissolve'). A new glyph part must either support material derivation or be excluded from recipe bases.

The work-level opt-ins live in 作品全体 → 見た目 (fields.js sec('look'): the repeat.same toggle「くり返しの行をそろえる」with offClears and noDice). There is no 作品全体 → 演出 section. Line-level choices live in 行 → 演出 (directionFields → repeatLineField).

renderer.js already builds both sides' scenes during a seam (seam.aCuts and seam.bCuts, items[].side) and blends the ground camera with textSeamCam. The glyph screen matrices of both sides are therefore available in one frame.
correctedGaps: There is no per-glyph morph where each character dissolves into the one that takes its place. blendDissolve and sumiSeep work on two whole composited text layers.

The surveyor's design is sound: a new seam that matches graphemes in screen space inside renderer.js, is pinned per boundary, is pool:false at first, and uses replaces {depart, arrive}. Corrections:

(1) Contract. Do not add a new scope 'glyph'. That touches registry.js:259, decideSeam's req.scope, the renderer's split and textSeamCam branches, and DESIGN §4.18.2. Instead keep scope 'text' and add an optional, additive hook such as morph(gx, A, B, u, p) that receives glyph lists. The renderer takes the glyph path only when def.morph exists, so the planner's scope logic and existing seams stay untouched. Add a DESIGN §4.18.2 row, a §5.9 Transitions catalog row (catalog.test.js reads the §5 tables), and a §4.19.2 step-4 addendum.

(2) Goldens.
- pool:false keeps auto picks and frame_hashes_v2 unchanged, provided the renderer emits no new ops or property sets when the seam is absent (the recorder logs every one).
- The new part still changes registry.version, and with it every fp and plan.hash. Regenerate plan_hashes.json, frame_hashes.json (registry field) and project_media.json, project_repeat.json and project_extreme.json on purpose with tests/update_golden.js, and record this in NOTES.
- Update the wording of the lens_filter_seam.test.js:125 assertion message ('every transition is an auto pick').

(3) The replaces.arrive branch in tracks.js has never been exercised. Add planner tests showing that A's depart becomes instantHide and B's arrive becomes instantShow with from:'rule', and that pins still win (replaceMotion skips pinned slots).

(4) Matching rule. Keep it pure and deterministic: LCS over graphemes in reading order, ties broken by nearest screen position and then by index. Compute it once per seam from the two cuts' texts, not per frame. Morph only when the overlap is meaningful, for example at least 2 shared graphemes in a run or at least 40% of the shorter line. - Compute overlap only when the toggle is on, so other documents' fingerprints do not change.
- The window likely needs its own clamp above SEAM_SHARE. That ends A earlier via endWithSeam.

(6) Also handle:

- EXTREME cover grounds and motion-blur copies (project_extreme).
- マイ素材 recipes: exclude the part as a base or support it.

(7) A cheaper first step is a per-glyph 'cross-melt': glyph pairs at the same reading index blur and crossfade in place without moving, and unmatched glyphs dissolve. It needs the same glyph access but no transform interpolation.
