survey.designNotes: Two engine options; B is preferred where the font supports it, with A as the fallback. (A) Stroke emboldening: append a pose column, e.g. 'bold' (ADD rule, em units), to table.js POSE. POSE is marked FROZEN, so this needs a DESIGN addendum, and identity 0 keeps existing scenes identical. In draw.js, the direct path does fillText and then strokeText in the same ink with lineWidth = 2·bold·em and a round join. In sprites.js, the sprite key gains a quantized bold level. This works with every font, including system fallbacks, and is deterministic, but it can only thicken. (B) Variable weight: a 'wght' pose column (ADD, in weight units). faces.js marks variable families and their ranges (e.g. Noto Sans JP, Murecho, Inter, Fraunces, Work Sans), and cssUrls requests a `wght@min..max` range only when a document uses a weight-animating part, so font URLs of other documents do not change. The draw path sets ctx.font with the weight quantized (e.g. steps of 25); glyphs are laid out once at the base weight and drawn centred in their cells, so nothing reflows. Families without an axis, and system fallbacks, step between served weights or fall back to A. Part: the entrance identity rule (kit.js: an entrance's tracks END at identity) means 細→太 is written as an arrive `weightGrow` 「太り」 with track wght [-k, 0] ending at the face's base weight, which should be heavy (700-900). Add K.mirror for a matching exit 「細り」 and optionally a hold 「太さの呼吸」 that pulses on beats. Gating: register the parts with pool:false (pin-only) or behind an opt-in, so auto picks and font requests of existing documents do not change and frame_hashes_v2 stays byte-identical (verify with frame.test.js). UI: 行/カット → 演出 → 入り (and 見せ/抜け) part picker, with params such as 始まりの太さ. Labels come from the part's L(ja, en), plus DESIGN §5.7 catalog table rows (docs tests read them). Tests: conformance.test.js identity rule, parts_motion.test.js, draw/sprite op tests with the recording context (font weight sequence or stroke width), a faces.test.js cssUrls range case, a browser glyph_parity check at intermediate weights, and export font readiness via engine/host/fonts.js for the whole range.
risks: Google Fonts CSS2 fails the whole request (HTTP 400) for a range or weight a family does not serve. We must know exactly which families are variable, and how variable axes behave with `text=` subsetting.

Canvas2D support for variable fonts, and its speed, differ between Chrome, Safari and Firefox. Changing ctx.font every frame creates many font instances, and the sprite cache (keyed by font css) can grow.
Offline, blocked or system-fallback fonts have only a few weights, so the animation steps instead of flowing.
Advance widths change with weight: Latin and proportional glyphs may overlap unless glyphs stay centred in fixed cells; reflowing is not acceptable.
Stroke emulation (option A) fills the counters of small kana and dense kanji at large widths, and it cannot make text thinner than the base weight.
Changing the FROZEN POSE list and the draw path must keep §4.19.5 preview/export parity and leave existing frames byte-identical (frame_hashes_v2).

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute 'missing' by searching wght, fontWeight, embolden, stroke width, lineWidth, thick and 太 across src/engine and src/parts. The only weight code is the static face weight: faces.js FAMILY_ROWS and cssUrls with discrete ':wght@w1;w2', snapWeight, and fields.js face.<role>.weight at 作品全体 → 書体 (fld.faceWeight 太さ（{role}）).

table.js POSE is the FROZEN list of 22 columns, none of which is a weight. sprites.js OUTLINE_WIDTH=0.045 em is a constant.

The look-alikes do not change weight: bloomOpen (scale plus glow), inkRise and fogIn (blur clears), thumpSwell and breathePulse (scale), creepTrack (letter spacing), and the echo column (chroma ghost copies at ±0.08 em in draw.js drawDirect).

Per line, the only lever is the static face role (text.face: display, serif, body), and each role has one weight for the whole video. Missing stands.
extraEvidence: The kit identity rule (parts/kit.js:194/210; conformance.test.js checkIdentity): an entrance's tracks must END at identity. A 細→太 entrance can only end at the cut's base weight. The base weight is per role for the whole video (DEFAULT_FACE weight 500 in faces.js:118), so 'thin → bold' also needs a bold base or a new per-cut or per-line weight value, which does not exist (CUT_NAMES and TEXT_SLOTS: text.face, scale, ink and style only).

DESIGN §4.19.5 (FROZEN): the direct or sprite path is chosen only from blur, glow, shard and pixel. The sprite key includes the font css, so every distinct weight becomes its own sprite in the 96 MB LRU cache.

engine/render/record.js logs every property set (font, lineWidth, lineJoin and others). Any new unconditional state set, or a change in the font css format from font.css(px), changes op hashes and breaks frame_hashes_v2.

NOTES.md WP2 (day-one font check): a weight a family does not serve makes the whole CSS2 request fail with HTTP 400 (e.g. DM Serif Display:wght@700), and families outside FAMILIES (a user's face pin) are requested with no weight axis at all.
The closest look-alikes are bloomOpen 花開き (grow plus glow), inkRise 墨のぼり (blur clears) and the glow column. None thicken strokes.
correctedGaps: No entrance, hold or exit animates stroke weight or thickness.
Weight is not animatable anywhere: no pose column and no draw path (no stroke emboldening, variable wght interpolation or crossfade between weights).
Fonts load at fixed served weights only (discrete :wght@ list with text= subsets), and each face role has one weight for the whole video.
No per-line or per-cut weight value exists. Combined with the entrance identity rule, even a new 'thin → base' entrance cannot end bolder than the whole-video role weight.
verdict.designCorrections:
The surveyor's options A (stroke emboldening) and B (variable wght) are reasonable, but:

(1) The catalog rows belong in DESIGN §5.2 Entrances, §5.3 Holds and §5.4 Exits. §5.7 is Cameras (lens). catalog.test.js checks the §5 tables against the registry.

(2) Add option C: crossfade between two served static weights, the way §4.19.5 already crossfades blur levels (alpha 1−f and f), with glyphs centred in their fixed cells.
- It needs no variable fonts and works with FAMILY_ROWS' discrete weights and text= subsets.
- It works on both draw paths, because the sprite key already includes the font css.
- The cost is a slight double edge mid-fade.
- It is the safest first step, with A as the fallback for families that serve only one weight.

(3) Font loading. faces.fontUsage and cssUrls must request the extra weights (or a wght range) only for documents that use a weight part. Other documents' font URLs, and export font readiness via engine/host/fonts.js, then stay unchanged. The facade computes font usage from scenes, so the part must declare the weights it will draw.

(4) The end weight. Arrive tracks must end at identity, so there are two choices:
- Add an optional cut or line value such as text.weight: a new SLOT_SPECS entry in cast.js, commands.js TEXT_SLOTS, fields.js CUT_NAMES, and fields in 行 → 色と書体 and カット → 文字. It is absent by default, so v2 plans are unchanged.
- Or let the part raise the weight for the whole cut, which needs a kit exception and a DESIGN addendum.

(5) POSE. Appending a column changes the FROZEN list of 22 (table.js POSE, ADD and IDENTITY, the stride of every table, scene/budget). It needs a DESIGN addendum and contract.test.js updates. An alternative that leaves POSE alone is a per-glyph draw override set by a behaviour, if the builder can carry one. Either way, when the value is identity (0) the draw path must not emit any new op or property set.

(6) Goldens. New parts with pool:false keep auto picks, and so frame_hashes_v2, unchanged. registry.version still changes, so regenerate plan_hashes.json, frame_hashes.json and the project_*.json goldens on purpose with update_golden.js.

(7) Tests: conformance (identity rule), parts_motion, recorder-op tests (the font weight sequence, or strokeText and lineWidth for option A), a faces.test.js cssUrls case showing extra weights only when used, and the browser glyph_parity check at intermediate weights.

(8) UI entry: 行 or カット → 演出 → the 入り, 見せ and 抜け part picker, with params 始まりの太さ and 終わりの太さ. The parts' L(ja, en) labels and blurbs serve as the UI strings. None of this needs AI.

survey.request: 声より0.2秒先に文字を出す
survey.summary: A lead offset already exists: the work setting timing.lead (作品全体 › タイミング › 入りの早さ) starts every cut's entrance that many seconds before the sung start. Its default is 0.12 s, not 0.2 s. It also only sets when the entrance begins: with the default, text finishes arriving about 0.4–0.5 s after the voice (median), so it is not readable before the voice.
evidence: src/core/timing.js TIMING_DEFAULTS = { snap:'off', lead: 0.12, tail: 0.25, leadIn: 1, outro: 2, tapLatency: 0.06 }
src/core/doc.js defaultDoc(): timing.lead 0.12; checkTiming() requires a number ≥ 0 (every saved doc stores the key)
src/planner/segment.js windows(): c.a = q6(c.t0 - timing.lead) is the cut's visible-from time; c.b = next.t0 + tail
src/engine/scene/build.js timesOf()/fitTimes(): the entrance runs from times.a (= -lead, cut-local) to rest = a + BH.motionTotal(...), so the arrive starts `lead` seconds before the sung start

DESIGN.md §3 (line ~404): 'lead (entrance starts this many seconds before the sung start)'. DESIGN §4.17 stagger 'sung' order: per-unit delays are counted from t0 − lead, so the per-glyph timing also leads
src/ui/fields.js sec('timing'): F({ cmd:{t:'timing.set',key:'lead'}, scopes: WORK, widget:'number', label:'fld.lead', spec: SPEC.timing }) where SPEC.timing is 0–10 s, step 0.01, not advanced-only
src/i18n/strings.js 'fld.lead': ['入りの早さ','Entrance lead'], 'sec.timing': ['タイミング','Timing']. src/core/commands.js TIMING_KEYS includes 'lead' (timing.set, undoable)
src/ui/tap.js eventTime(): tap times already subtract timing.tapLatency (0.06), so t0 is close to the real sung onset

Measured with a read-only scratch script $SCRATCH/survey/t4_lead.js (planner + buildCut, fixtures basic/lrc/long/vertical, lead 0.12). Every line cut has a = -0.120. Entrance end relative to the sung start: p50 +0.43…+0.53 s, p90 +0.57…+0.91 s. Only 11 of 304 cuts are fully in before the voice
tests/fixtures/project_*.json all store timing.lead 0.12 explicitly. tests/node/doc.test.js:27 asserts the default timing object
survey.userPath: 作品全体 › タイミング › 入りの早さ に 0.2 を入力する（初期値は 0.12 秒）。「元に戻す」で戻せます。
gaps: The default is 0.12 s. The owner wants 0.2 s, and nothing suggests or explains that value; the field has no note.

lead only moves the start of the entrance. The text is fully readable only after the arrive finishes (about 0.3–0.9 s later), so with any lead ≤ 0.2 most lines are still animating in when the voice starts. No mode exists for 'text readable N s before the voice'.
It is a single work-wide value: no per-line or per-cut override, and no automatic scaling with entrance length or tempo.
survey.designNotes:
Two options, both safe for frame_hashes_v2.
(A) Minimal: change core/doc defaultDoc().timing.lead (and core/timing TIMING_DEFAULTS) to 0.2 for new documents only. Every fixture (and so frame_hashes_v2, plan_hashes, corpus) stores lead 0.12 explicitly, so the goldens stay byte-identical. Documents already saved keep their stored value. Also: update tests/node/doc.test.js:27, DESIGN.md §3 example and the defaultDoc() description, and the first-run sample (it uses defaultDoc). Relabel or annotate the field, e.g. add a 'fld.lead.note' such as 「声より何秒先に文字が動き始めるか（0.2秒前後が読みやすい）」 in strings.js [ja,en], and possibly offer a 0.2 preset.
(B) Real 'readable before the voice': add an optional timing key (e.g. timing.ready, absent means today's behaviour; add it to core/doc ORDER.timing, TIMING_NUMBERS and commands TIMING_KEYS). planner/segment.windows then sets a = t0 − max(lead, ready + A_est), where A_est is the arrive slot's dur + each·(units−1) taken from the cast params. The engine needs no change because fitTimes reads cut.a. Clamp a so it never goes earlier than the previous cut's t0 + a minimum, to keep the 'overlaps only neighbours' invariant (engine/scene/budget.js, DESIGN_2_1 §2059). It stays deterministic because it is a pure planner function of doc + registry. UI: a toggle or number in 作品全体 › タイミング. Tests: segment/timing tests that a = t0 − lead when unset; a new test for ready; ui_fields test for the new field.
risks: DESIGN_2_1 §14 whipPan (EXTREME x-shot) uses a hard-coded b − .37 … b − .25 window that 'equals the next cut's lead window with the default timing (lead 0.12)'. With 0.2 the whips of A and B no longer coincide exactly.
A larger lead (especially option B) increases the overlap between consecutive cuts: two lines on screen at once, busier frames, and pressure on budget.js and area assumptions for short lines.

Changing the default for new documents changes the first-run sample look and any test built from D.defaultDoc(). Changing it for existing documents would break frame_hashes_v2, so the change must not be applied through migrate/normalize.
engine/facade.js SAMPLE (lead 0.12) for part thumbnails is separate and would disagree with the new default (cosmetic only).

verdict.reasoning: I checked every cited fact and they hold. core/timing.js TIMING_DEFAULTS and core/doc.js defaultDoc() both set lead 0.12. segment.windows() sets c.a = q6(c.t0 - timing.lead) for every cut, including title, interlude and outro cuts. build.js timesOf()/fitTimes() start the entrance at a and set rest = a + BH.motionTotal. The field 入りの早さ (fields.js:313, WORK scope, SPEC.timing 0–10 s) sits in the collapsed タイミング section of 詳細 › 作品全体 and is not advanced-only. I re-ran $SCRATCH/survey/t4_lead.js and got the same numbers: a = -0.120 on every line cut, arrive end p50 +0.43…+0.53 s after the sung start, and 11 of 304 cuts fully in before the voice. The status stays partial. Typing 0.2 does exactly what the sentence says (the entrance starts 0.2 s before the voice), but the owner asks for this 定石 to be built in, and the default is 0.12 with nothing pointing users to 0.2. The design notes need fixing in two places. Option A as written would leak into existing documents. Option B is placed in the wrong pipeline stage.
extraEvidence: planner/plan.js:513 builds ctx.timing = Object.assign({}, TM.TIMING_DEFAULTS, doc.timing). Changing TIMING_DEFAULTS changes the plan of any document planned without the key (many node tests build docs directly).

core/doc.js:338-356 normalize() uses defaultDoc() as its fill base (fillMissing(v, base[k])). A saved or hand-made file that lacks timing.lead gets whatever defaultDoc() says, so changing defaultDoc() changes such files. migrate.parseFile always runs D.normalize.

plan.js pipeline: SG.cutAll (step 3, where windows() sets a) runs before CA.castCut (step 5). The arrive part and its dur/each are not known when a is set, and behave.motionTiming fits dur/each to the window span b − a via MO.fitMotion.
export/subtitles.js srt(): cue start = item.t0 (the sung start). The SRT subtitles (on by default in the Filmora kit) and LRC ignore lead, so subtitles appear exactly on the voice.

core/shot.js:302-304 and :638 whipPan: A's whip-out keys at b − .37 … b − .25 (= next.t0 − 0.12 … next.t0 with tail 0.25). B's whip-in runs at a … a + 0.1 (= t0 − lead …). DESIGN_2_1:5526 relies on lead 0.12.

NOTES ~3210 / engine/render/post.whenWeight: the 'arrive' effect weight falls over 0.2 s from rest (= a on instant entrances). With lead 0.2, flashPop/invertBlink arrive flashes are gone by the sung start.
parts/lens/kick.js:134 impactKick uses pre: 0.12, measured from the sung start and not from a. It is independent of lead (fine).
fields.js:292 shows an F({ note: 'fld.repeatSame.note' }) mechanism already exists, so a 'fld.lead.note' needs no new widget code.
tests/golden frame_hashes_v2 corpus = PROJECTS ['basic','vertical','lrc','long'] (tests/helpers/corpus.js). All of them store timing.lead 0.12 explicitly.
correctedGaps: The default lead is 0.12 s, not 0.2 s. Nothing in the UI (no note, no preset) says that about 0.2 s ahead is the recommended value.

lead only moves the start of the entrance. With the auto arrive (dur 0.35–0.8 s, each 0.02–0.07 s, core/registry.js motionShared) the text is fully in only about 0.3–0.9 s after the voice (p50 +0.43…+0.53 s). No option says 'text readable N s before the voice'.
It is one work-wide value. There is no per-line or per-cut lead (only the arrive 長さ/ずらし can be pinned per line or cut to shorten the entrance).
Subtitle export (SRT, and LRC by nature) uses the sung t0 and does not lead.
verdict.designCorrections: (A) New works only. Do not change core/timing TIMING_DEFAULTS, and do not let D.normalize fill 0.2: normalize uses defaultDoc() as its fill base, so a file without timing.lead would silently change. Keep the fill value at 0.12 (e.g. a LEGACY/FILL timing constant used by normalize and TIMING_DEFAULTS). Give 0.2 only where a new work is created: a D.newDoc(), or defaultDoc({ fresh: true }) used by ui/boot.js:107 (store init), project_io.js:610 (新規) and :1176 (first run / sample). The fixtures store 0.12, so frame_hashes_v2, plan_hashes and project_repeat stay byte-identical. Update doc.test.js:27 and review the ~20 node tests that plan D.defaultDoc() documents (planner_pins, ui_fields, ai_song, commands, …) for assertions on a = t0 − 0.12 or whip timing. Add 'fld.lead.note' [ja,en] through the existing F({ note }) field option, and optionally a 0.2 preset. (B) 'Readable before the voice' cannot go in segment.windows(). windows() runs in the cutter (plan step 3), before cast (step 5) picks the arrive part and its dur/each, and fitMotion fits dur/each to b − a, so deriving a from the fitted arrive is circular. Put it in the engine instead: an optional timing key (e.g. timing.ready; absent means today's behaviour) that engine/scene/build.js fitTimes / behave.motionTiming uses to fit the arrive into [a, −ready] instead of the whole window (so it only works when lead > ready, e.g. lead 0.5, ready 0.2). Or use a planner post-cast pass that widens c.a before encoding. Either way the value must reach the cut encoding (encode.js:201 already keys on 'window lead') so caches invalidate. Absent key means byte-identical output. Add it to core/doc ORDER.timing, TIMING_NUMBERS and commands TIMING_KEYS, and put the UI in 作品全体 › タイミング. If subtitles should also lead, that is a separate opt-in in export/subtitles (tests export_kit / subtitles), never a default change.

survey.request: 曲から行の頭を自動で下書き
survey.summary: The app can already draft every line's start time from the song's audio, but only through AI: 「AIでタイミング」 sends the audio and numbered lines to Gemini, and the user reviews the proposed start pins before applying them. AI transcription with times also exists. Without AI there is no audio-based line-start detection. Automatic timing only spreads lines by text length and reading rate (from the BPM), with optional beat snap.
evidence: src/ai/song.js alignRequest()/ALIGN_SCHEMA/alignChanges(): Gemini returns { i, start } per line. The result becomes review changes (kind 'time', path line/<id>:start, pins by 'ai', overLrc flag), with strictly increasing times and a move of ≥ 0.05 s
src/ai/song.js transcribeRequest()/transcriptLines(): lyrics transcribed from audio with [mm:ss.xx] start stamps (another AI-only way to get line heads)

src/ui/ai_controller.js songBlocked(): 'ai.song.onlyGemini' (the provider must take audio), 'ai.song.noSong', 'ai.song.notLinked'. blocked(): requires an API key and hasConsent() ('ai.song.needConsent')

src/ui/step_song.js aiBtn 「AIでタイミング」 (data-act 'ai.align'): hidden unless view.state.prefs.ai, disabled without doc.song (tooltip 'song.aiNeedsSong'). src/ui/boot.js def('ai.align', …, enabled: prefs.ai && doc.song)

src/audio/analyze.js computes only a loudness envelope and onset strength (spectral flux) at 100 Hz plus tempo and offset. There is no vocal-activity or phrase detection, and the onset strength is used only for the BPM
src/audio/digest.js songRecord(): only a 20 Hz loudness digest is kept in doc.song. src/ui/boot.js keeps app.buffer (decoded audio) but not the analysis

src/core/timing.js solveTimes(): with no anchors, forwardFill() from leadIn at morae/readRate (readRate = clamp(bpm/20, 3, 14)), compressed to song length − outro. snapAutoStarts() snaps to the beat grid when 拍に合わせる is on. This is text-based, not onset-based
A grep for vocal/silence/detect/draft/phrase in src finds no audio line-start detector
docs/SPEC.md §4: 'Automatic start times from text length (and BPM when known) … LRC import; AI alignment'
survey.userPath: ② 曲 で曲を読み込む → ≡メニューの設定でAIを有効にし、Geminiのキーを入れる → ② 曲 の「AIでタイミング」（AIパネル）→ 曲の送信に同意 → 提案を確認して適用。AIなしでは、行は文字数・読む速さ・テンポから自動で並ぶだけです（拍に合わせる で拍へ寄せる）。
gaps: No non-AI path: without a Gemini key, provider and consent, nothing looks at the audio to find where lines start (a requirement: everything must work without AI).
AI align needs Gemini specifically (a assistant key is refused with ai.song.onlyGemini) and needs the song linked in this session (decoded buffer).
The own analysis (onset strength, envelope at 100 Hz) is discarded after load; there is no vocal-band or phrase-gap feature to build on.
survey.designNotes:
Add an opt-in, deterministic, non-AI 「曲から下書き」.
1) New pure L1 module src/audio/phrases.js (deps: audio/fft), run on app.buffer in idle slices like audio/host/decode.analyzeBuffer, with progress and 中止. It computes per 10 ms frame a vocal-activity curve: vocal-band (~200–4000 Hz) energy of the mid channel minus the side channel (center-panned vocals); for mono, band energy × harmonicity. From that it finds candidate phrase onsets: rises after low-activity gaps ≥ ~150 ms, sharpened by the onset strength, each with a score.
2) A pure aligner (e.g. core/draft.js or inside the same module): dynamic programming that assigns the lines whose start is 'auto' (plan.lines[i].by.start === 'auto') to an increasing subsequence of candidates. Cost = −score + λ·|gap − expected| (expected = morae/readRate + pause, as in core/timing). Existing pins and LRC anchors stay fixed as constraints, and it respects timing's 0.1 s ANCHOR_GAP.
3) Output: either (a) one undoable batch of pins with label 「曲から下書き（n行）」, or (b) an in-app review reusing ai/changes CH.make kind 'time' and the ai_review list without a provider. Pin 'by': core/doc PIN_BY is ['user','ai','tap','lock']. Adding 'draft' changes validation (older builds would refuse such files), so either reuse 'tap'/'user' or write the draft as LRC stamps via lyrics.set (the lowest-precedence source, so later taps and pins win: pin > LRC > auto; menus.bakeTimes already writes stamps).
4) UI: a button in ② 曲 next to 「タップで合わせる」, enabled when app.songReady(), with strings song.draft / song.draftHint / undo.draft [ja,en]; then suggest 「タップで打ち直し」 for bad lines.
5) frame_hashes_v2 is unaffected because this runs only on a user action and stores pins or stamps.
6) Tests: node tests with synthetic WAVs (tests/helpers/media_gen.js style: tone bursts at known times over noise and clicks) that check detected onsets within ±0.15 s; aligner unit tests (keeps pins and LRC, strictly increasing, deterministic); a ui_flows step for the button and its undo.
risks: Accuracy on real mixes: vocals not centered, reverb and doubles, backing vocals, rap without gaps, and instrumental hits taken for vocal onsets. It must be presented as a 下書き (draft) to fix with taps.
Needs the decoded buffer: after reopening a project the song must be relinked first (same limitation as AI align, 'ai.song.notLinked').
Cost: one more FFT pass over the whole song (similar to the load-time analysis). It must run in slices with cancel so the UI does not freeze on long songs.
Overwriting: it must never silently replace user, tap or AI pins or LRC stamps; only fill auto lines unless the user confirms.
Adding a new pin 'by' value is a schema and validation change (core/doc PIN_BY) with forward-compatibility cost.

verdict.reasoning: I confirmed the AI-only path. ai/song.js alignRequest/ALIGN_SCHEMA/alignChanges produce 'time' changes with pins on line/<id>:start (requires strictly increasing times and a move of ≥ 0.05 s). transcribeRequest/transcriptLines give [mm:ss.xx] stamps. ai_controller.songBlocked refuses a non-audio provider (providers.js: only Gemini has audio: true), a missing song, and a song that is not linked; blocked() requires consent. step_song.js hides 「AIでタイミング」 unless prefs.ai. Without AI nothing uses the audio to find line starts. audio/analyze.js computes the envelope and onset strength only to estimate tempo and offset. host/decode.loadSong returns the analysis, but boot keeps only buffer, peaks and the songRecord (20 Hz loudness digest). core/timing.solveTimes gets songSeconds, bpm, grid and readRate, never the digest or onsets. The timeline has no onset snapping (timeline.js snapTime uses beats and line edges). Manual tap-sync is the only non-AI way to take line heads from the song, and it is not automatic. So partial is right: an automatic draft exists only through optional AI.
extraEvidence: planner/plan.js:66-70 timeLines(): the solveTimes context contains no audio features. core/timing forwardFill starts at max(titleCard, leadIn=1 s), not at the first vocal.

audio/host/decode.js:76-84 loadSong returns { buffer, song, analysis, peaks }. ui/boot.js keeps app.setSongBuffer(buffer) and app.peaks only. On relink (boot.js ~511) the song is decoded but not analyzed again.
tests/fixtures/project_basic.json (in the frame_hashes_v2 corpus) has song.seconds 60 with a digest and 0 pins: every line start is auto.
core/doc.js:17 PIN_BY = ['user','ai','tap','lock']. doc.js:210 validate refuses any other 'by' (an older build would report 'invalid', not 'newer').
boot.js def('panel.ai') and def('ai.align') are enabled only when view.state.prefs.ai, so the AI review list (ui/ai_review) is unreachable with AI off.
core/tap.js MIN_GAP 0.12 vs core/timing ANCHOR_GAP 0.1: timing demotes an anchor closer than 0.1 s to the previous one (time-order).
ui/menus.js:146 bakeTimes writes LRC stamps and clears every line start pin. A draft must not copy that pin clearing.

verdict.reasoning: The mechanism exists as described. ui/tap.start() begins at the selected line (S.lineOfSel), seeks 2 s before it (PREROLL) and plays. core/tap.tapCommand emits only marked lines. Esc / T / 終わる dispatch one time.tap (undo 'タップで合わせる（1行）'). commands.timeTap writes pins by 'tap' only for those marks. The S key, the [今] button (widgets.js:244) and timeline edge drags also exist. But the owner's words '1行だけ' are not what the tap flow does, and re-timing one line has a correctness defect. (a) No one-line mode: the button hint is 「{n}行から・スペースで記録」 (from line n on), the panel moves on to 「次: …」 and keeps playing, and a second tap re-marks the next line. Stopping after one line is left to the user. (b) A stale end pin breaks the re-tap. timeTap sets only the start, and solveTimes takes t1 = max(endPin, t0 + 0.2). End pins are common: E during tap, a timeline body drag, the inspector time shift (both use time.shift, which pins start AND end by 'user') and the 終了 field. I checked it with a scratch script ($SCRATCH/survey/sk_s2_endpin.js): line r3 pinned 8–10.5, re-tapped at 11, becomes 11–11.2 s with no warning. The tap report() only checks by.start, so nothing is said. (c) When neighbours are auto, re-tapping one line re-spreads them (timing.spread/backFill): re-tapping r2 from 5 to 7 moved r1, r3 and r4 too. So the core exists, but '1行だけ打ち直し' as a reliable, discoverable action is not complete.

verdict.designCorrections: Treat it as a small completion, not new architecture. (1) Correctness first, in core/commands timeTap, which is pure and sees the doc. When a mark sets a start without an end and the line's existing end pin is ≤ start + 0.2 (core/timing MIN_LEN), either clear that end pin or move it by the same delta so the line keeps its length. Say which in DESIGN §4.11, and name the dropped end in the tap report() toast. Tests: commands.test.js and tap.test.js, plus a ui_flows retap step with a prior timeline drag. (2) One-line mode in ui/tap: start({ only: lineId }). After the first accepted mark, keep playing until the next line's t0 so E can still mark the end, then auto-finish (the same finish(), one time.tap). Optionally loop the 2 s pre-roll until a mark. core/tap can stay unchanged, or gain a pure 'stopAfter' index in TapState (tap.test.js). (3) Entry points: a 「タップ」 button beside [今] on 詳細 › 行 › 開始 (widgets.time), a line context menu on the timeline (currently only bandMenu), a palette command 'tap.line' and maybe Shift+T. Strings tap.onlyLine / tap.onlyHint / song.tapLine [ja,en]; change the ② 曲 hint to mention stopping with Esc. (4) Optionally warn in the toast when auto neighbours moved, or offer to pin the neighbours' current starts first. survey.summary: The app can already reveal text one glyph (or word) at a time on the singing's schedule: 文字の出方 has the option 歌に合わせて (order 'sung'). Each unit starts at its estimated sung time, (morae before it ÷ all morae) × the cut's length, and 入り「打鍵」 gives a character-by-character reveal paced over the line. But these times are a guess based on counting sounds, not per-character timing taken from the song. The app has no source of word or character timing (enhanced-LRC word tags are thrown away, the AI align returns line starts only, and tap records line starts and ends only). There is also no one-step 歌ハメ switch or karaoke-style highlight, and the planner never chooses 'sung' by itself.

survey.designNotes: 1) Where the times come from. Store everything in the doc so rendering stays deterministic and needs neither the song file nor AI. (a) Enhanced-LRC word tags: add an optional field to core/lyrics ParsedRow, e.g. syncs [{at: text index, t}], leaving `text` unchanged so lyrics.test.js still holds. Carry it on Line and slice it per cut in planner/segment attach() as cut-local unit times. Add the field only when present, and include it in the cut fingerprint. (b) Per-character tap without AI: extend the core/tap reducer with a sub-mark event, started from a new 「1字ずつタップ」 button on the 行 page (時間 section). It loops the line (optionally slowed) and marks each mora, grapheme or breaker word. Save the result as a line pin line/<id>:sync (offsets from the line start), validated like split pins: after a text edit, emit pin-bad-value and fall back to the estimate. (c) Optional AI: an ai/song align variant returning per-word starts as 'ai' pins through the existing review UI. (d) Optional no-AI refinement: end the spread at the vocal end using the loudness digest, or persist onset peaks in doc.song and snap mora boundaries to them. This must be opt-in because it changes 'sung' frames. 2) Engine: in behave.motionTiming's 'sung' branch, use the cut's sync times when present (delay_j = t_unit − times.a, clamped to [0, room]), otherwise keep sungFractions. Reuse 'sung' rather than adding an ORDERS value (the list is FROZEN in contract.test.js). This needs a glyph → source-text-index map in the layout target (engine/text/layout), because giantWhisper, vertical text and latin words reorder or merge units. Leave sungFractions as used by shot/xshot anchors (emph, reading, word:k) alone, or upgrade it under the same gate. 3) A 歌ハメ switch: a work pin, off by default, under 作品全体 › タイミング or 見た目, plus the same on the 行 and 区画 pages. When on, the planner (planner/cast, like the repeat.same opt-in) pins a fast per-glyph entrance (typeOn or a quick pop) with order 'sung'. An optional karaoke-fill dwell part must use pool:false so v2 automatic choices do not change. 4) frame_hashes_v2 stays byte-identical because nothing changes unless 'sung' is pinned or the switch is on, and no fixture pins 'sung'. The lrc fixture's word tags must not be used by default. If syncs enter the plan, plan_hashes.json for 'lrc' needs a refresh (not frozen); gate it to avoid that. 5) Strings: fld.utahame / .note, tap.sync.* (start, progress, done), warn.sync-mismatch, in ja/en pairs. 6) Tests: frame.test.js (sung delays follow sync, fallback when there is none), lyrics.test.js (tags parsed, text unchanged), tap.test.js (sub-marks, back, MIN_GAP), planner (plans unchanged without the opt-in; slicing per cut), ui_fields.test.js (new field), ui_flows.py (per-character tap flow), and the existing frame_hashes_v2 check (frame.test.js:239).
risks: The FROZEN goldens: frame_hashes_v2 includes project_lrc, whose rows carry <mm:ss> word tags. Using them automatically would change v2 frames, so they must be gated.
Mapping glyphs to text indices is fragile: layouts reorder units (giantWhisper, NOTES:7891), vertical text and particles, latin words, and merged pieces ('piece-merged').
Sync data goes stale when lyrics or splits are edited; it needs validation and a fallback to the estimate.
Tapping every character live is very hard in fast songs. Offer per-word or per-mora units and slowed playback.
It interacts with timing.lead (text shows 0.12 s early) and with the owner's separate '0.2秒先' item. The two need one consistent rule.
The camera's reading paths (shot.js / xshot.js use sungFractions) would drift from the text if only the stagger switched to real times.
Adding a new automatically chosen part or order value would change v2 part choices or break the contract test.

Mostly sound. Corrections and additions:
(1) Enhanced-LRC tags are absolute times tied to one stamp. A row with several stamps is sung several times (lines r7, r7.1), and a line whose start was re-pinned by tap or AI no longer matches the tag times. Store sync as offsets from the row's first stamp and apply them to every occurrence. Drop them (with a warning) when an offset falls outside that occurrence's t0..t1.
(2) Gating must cover every consumer of the estimate, not only the stagger:
- stagger/behave
- engine/scene/shot sungOf and xshot reading keys: camera is off in v2 goldens, but frame_hashes.json (not frozen) would change
- parts/ornament/mark underSweep sungShare: underSweep is chosen automatically in v2 plans (the paper and earth themes weight it) and draws with the camera off, so feeding it the lrc fixture's word tag automatically could break frame_hashes_v2 for 'lrc'.
Keep all of them on the old estimate unless the opt-in pin is set. Unify the estimate behind one helper, so a future real-sync path changes all consumers together.
(3) Do not touch SHARED.arrive.order auto (registry.js:59) or any part's shared auto. That would shift v2 choices and plan hashes. The 歌ハメ switch must override the order param and filter the arrive pool only when its pin resolves, mirroring cast.js REPEAT 'repeat.same' (acceptRepeat, alignments), so per-slot RNG streams stay unchanged without it.
(4) A new line slot 'sync' is not free. It touches the pin path grammar (core/paths, core/pins), planner slot validation (pin-bad-value / pin-not-applicable), core/reconcile (pins follow rows on text edits), ui/inspector NO_DICE, and the ai_changes whitelist if AI may write it. The cut fingerprint (plan.js planCut) must include the sliced unit times. Because retimeCut reuses fingerprints for cuts that only moved in time, store the times relative to cut.t0 (cut-local).
(5) The planner's repT (MO.heroTime) ignores 'sung'. If the switch makes 'sung' common, repT should use the 'sung' total, but only under the gate, because repT is printed in the plan hash.
(6) A cheap no-new-data step: under the gate, cap the 'sung' spread at min(t1 − t0, morae/readRate), the estimated singing length, and surface tap mode's E (end marks) in the 歌ハメ help text. Changing the existing 'sung' formula without a gate would not break goldens (no fixture pins 'sung'), but it would silently change user projects that already pin it, so gate it or keep the old formula.
(7) Tests: also contract.test.js stays unchanged (ORDERS frozen), planner_stability (no plan changes without the pin), and an underSweep/shot check that they are unchanged without the opt-in.

survey.designNotes: Add a pure, deterministic check, readCheck(doc, plan), in a new module (e.g. planner/readable.js or ui/readcheck.js). Check each lyric cut, since each cut shows only its own piece: shown = cut.t1 − cut.t0, optionally minus the fitted entrance and exit (the engine's times.rest/out are more exact, but the planner-level figure is enough). The amount is S.morae(cut.text, cut.lang) for ja/ko and cells or syllables for latin. Flag when shown < about 0.6 s with at least 3 cells, or rate > about 11–12 units/s. DESIGN's density normaliser, clamp(cps/12), already treats 12 cells/s as the top. Because automatic fills follow readRate (default 7), in practice flags come from tapped, LRC, AI or pinned times and from time-compressed fills; skip automatic lines unless the readRate pin itself is over the limit. Keep the result out of plan.warnings: planHash (planner/encode.js) hashes every top-level key, so a new warning would require refreshing plan_hashes.json. Compute it in the UI layer instead, the way output.checks is built. frame_hashes_v2 is unaffected either way because nothing is drawn. Where it shows: (1) the lyric editor gutter '!' via WARN_CODES, with the title from warn.too-fast; (2) the '!' in the 作品全体 › 行 list (inspector linesList); (3) a note under 行 › 時間 › 長さ, 「1秒に約{n}音 — 読み切れないかもしれません」, with quick fixes: 終わりを延ばす (line end pin), 区切りを減らす (fewer cuts), 入りの早さを上げる (timing.lead); (4) step ④ preflight item 'too-fast' at level 'info' with jump {cut} (export/schedule.warningItems, ui/output checkKey/FIX_LABELS); (5) optionally a toast after tap-sync ends, e.g. 「{n}行が速すぎるかもしれません」 (ui/tap.js, next to tap.doneSome). Surface time-compressed and piece-merged in the same places. Strings in ja/en pairs: warn.too-fast, exp.pre.too-fast, insp.readFast, tap.doneFast. Could be switched off in settings. Works fully without AI. Tests: a new tests/node/readcheck.test.js (thresholds, split cuts, latin, no flags for automatic lines at the default readRate, determinism), ui_output.test.js (preflight item and jump), the ui_fields line-page note, a ui_flows.py gutter '!' check, and the existing golden checks unchanged.
risks: Thresholds are subjective. Viewers hear the words, so lyric videos tolerate faster text than subtitles. Too strict a threshold floods every tapped chorus with '!'.
Estimates for English and mixed-script lines (syllable counting, latin cells) are rough.
Short shouted words or repeated one-word lines can be flagged falsely; a minimum cell count is needed.
Motion eats into reading time (long entrances or exits, EXTREME camerawork). A t1 − t0 check misses that, while the exact engine window is known only after scenes are built.

verdict.designCorrections:
Corrections to the proposed check:
(1) Include automatic lines. timing.spread() compresses them without warning between close anchors, and readRate can be pinned up to 14. Evaluate every lyric cut regardless of line.by.
(2) Measure over the legible window, not t1 − t0. Plan level: legible ≈ (b − L) − (a + A), with A and L from MO.fitMotion over cut.slots.arrive/depart p and feat.units (the same math as MO.heroTime; cut.repT already gives a + A + 10 %). Engine level (exact): times.out − times.rest from build.js fitTimes.
(3) Drop the absolute 'shown < 0.6 s' floor, or tie it to MIN_PIECE (0.35 s). On t1 − t0 it flags 76 of 1,441 automatic pieces that read at 7 morae/s. Use a rate rule, units / legible s > max(11, 1.6 × readRate), with a minimum of about 3 cells, and count latin by syllables or cells.
(4) Under order 'sung', A covers nearly the whole window (behave motionTiming), so legible ≈ 0 by design. Judge those cuts by t1 − t0 instead.
(5) Two architectures work:
- A pure UI or export check (like export/schedule flashRate and preflight).
- Better for exact times and zero plumbing: an engine scene warning modelled on overfullOf in engine/scene/build.js. It flows automatically to lyric_editor WARN_CODES (add 'too-fast'), the 行 list '!' and export warningItems (add a branch). It never enters plan.warnings, so planHash and plan_hashes.json are untouched. It draws nothing, so frame_hashes_v2 and frame_hashes stay byte-identical. The caveat is that scene warnings are known only for cuts the facade has laid out (it lays out unseen cuts in time slices), so preflight must wait for a full scan as it does for overfull.
The report's claim that a planner warning 'would require refreshing plan_hashes.json' is overstated: it changes hashes only where it fires, and no fixture reaches 11 morae/s.
(6) Add a title to the 行 list '!' (inspector.js:1440) with t('warn.'+code) for the first warning, and surface time-compressed and piece-merged with their existing strings. This is part of the same fix, UI-only and golden-safe.
(7) Quick fixes:
- 終わりを延ばす: a line/<id>:end pin, capped at the next start.
- 区切りを減らす: a split pin 'none'.
- 入りを短く: an arrive.dur pin, or 文字の出方 away from 'sung'.
- 読む速さ: work readRate, which only helps automatic lines.
Everything works without AI. Tests: add a spread()-squeezed case with anchors to the new readcheck or scene test, cover 'sung' cuts, and assert no flags on the fixture corpus at defaults.
